transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Lately, I keep thinking everyone would be better off without me, and I find myself planning how I might just not be here anymore. It just feels like too much, and a friend from the community center urged me to come speak with you.
Have you experienced these persistent feelings of hopelessness and low mood for at least two years, or is this a more recent change in how you've been feeling?

My general struggles and mood swings started about two years ago when my mother fell ill back home. But these specific heavy, low feelings and the thoughts of disappearing have really been happening on and off for about seven months now.
Have you experienced any similar periods of feeling this depressed or hopeless before these last seven months, or is this the first time you have felt this way?

No, this is actually the first time in my life I've ever felt this specific kind of deep depression. Before these last seven months, I had never experienced these heavy, hopeless feelings or thought about disappearing.
Over these past seven months, have you noticed significant changes in your sleep, appetite, or your ability to concentrate on daily tasks?

Yes, they have been completely all over the place. Some nights I only sleep two or three hours without feeling tired, and my eating swings from barely touching food to binging on rice and sweets at 2 a.m. Also, my concentration at work is terrible because I get so easily distracted by every little thing and leave tasks half-done.
During those periods where you were sleeping very little and feeling highly distracted, did you also feel unusually energetic, talkative, or feel like your thoughts were racing faster than normal?

Yes, during those times my head races incredibly fast with thoughts constantly crashing into each other. I feel this restless energy like I am powered by a motor I can't turn off, so I can't sit still and end up cleaning or starting multiple projects while my mind jumps around.

During those periods of high energy and racing thoughts, have you ever felt so out of control or disconnected from reality that you required hospitalization or had experiences that others couldn't see or hear?

I have never been hospitalized, but during those wired phases, I definitely experience things that others don't. The deep male voice telling me I'm a failure gets much louder, and the feeling that people are sending secret messages about me through their phones and the TV becomes almost constant.
Do you experience these voices and feelings of being watched only during the periods when your mood is very high or very low, or do they also happen when your mood is relatively stable?

Yes, they actually do happen even when my mood is relatively stable. For example, a few months ago when my mood felt more normal and neither high nor low, I was still convinced people were coordinating against me and I kept hearing that deep male voice at night.
To clarify, do you experience these voices and paranoid thoughts for at least two weeks in the absence of any significant mood symptoms (neither high nor low)?

Yes, that is exactly what happened. A few months ago, there was a stretch of about two or three weeks where my mood felt completely normal, not high or low at all. But even during those weeks, I was still hearing that deep voice at night and felt sure people were coordinating against me.
Looking back over the entire seven-month period, have the symptoms of your mood swings (the high energy or the deep depression) been present for the majority of the total duration of your illness?

Yes, looking back over the last couple of years, most of my time has been spent in that sped-up, high-energy mode or recovering from it. I have only had much shorter stretches where I felt normal or somewhere in the middle.
Over the seven-month period, would you say you have spent more time experiencing the high-energy, 'sped-up' symptoms, or have you spent more time experiencing the deep, hopeless depression?

Honestly, I have spent much more of my time in those sped-up, high-energy periods. While the heavy, depressed feelings have been coming and going for about seven months, those wired phases have actually been going on much longer—for about a year and eight months now. They have made up the vast majority of my time over these last couple of years.
During the periods when you were experiencing these 'sped-up' phases, did you also experience the deep, hopeless depression at the same time, or were those two states strictly separate?

They don't really happen at the same time; they usually alternate. It swings on me so that some weeks I feel strangely high, wired, and touchy, and then other weeks I crash and just feel flat, low, and empty inside.
